correctness.rationale: Exact nested rank-four first-order types use atomic equality/0/R diagrams and sets of one-point extension types, preserving arbitrary Boolean nesting and quantifier alternation; scaling is an automorphism. For a triple the only nongeneric fourth-move values belong to 19 rational linear forms. The rational arrangement has 60 primitive collision hyperplanes, 46 special-coordinate functions and 93 exceptional slopes. Their pairwise rational cross-determinants have prime divisors exactly all primes at most 131 and 157,191; denominator primes are small. For p>=193, exceptional slopes and generic choices stabilize, giving a four-round Duplicator strategy. Finite type recursion distinguishes each of 34 exceptional primes; targeted independent type computations confirm rank-four roots 137=193 and 157!=193, 191!=193. The source full finite program checks each prime through 193; our independent check did not replay all 47 cases, so that finite all-prime step relies on inspected executable algorithm, not our targeted spot tests. Relational language is essential; no result for a function symbol or composites.

originality.rationale: No located primary rank-four 35-class table. Gomaa 2007, Theorem 3.3, claims a lower bound m>=n+1 when 2^n<p<2^(n+1), apparently contrary to this explicit p=157 vs193 rank-four separation (n=7); the contradiction is acknowledged and not silently treated as supporting evidence. The thesis proof isolates a fixed binder form and does not visibly cover arbitrary alternating extension patterns. Exact type recursion and the arithmetic arrangement provide an independent reason for the contrary conclusion; however the conflicting published assertion is a high-priority residual scientific risk and not an established correction to Gomaa in general.
